Deleting only site-packages/vcr_patch.py (Dockerfile lines 30-47) makes run_tests.sh report 17 passed, 3 of 3 runs, while `socket.socket.setsockopt` is still <function patched_setsockopt>. _socket_intercept.py and the sitecustomize hook stay installed. The damage the instruction names ('modifications to TCP socket handling') is not checked at all.

vcr_patch raises randomly when random()<0.3 on each play_response. In the damaged state one run gave '7 failed, 10 passed', so the failure count varies from run to run. P(all 17 pass unrepaired) is at most about 0.7^17, roughly 0.002, so a false pass is rare. After a repair, grading is deterministic.

Red herring: /var/cache/kernel_tcp_backup.enc is an XOR-encrypted dump of /proc/sys/net. The key fragments on disk (/var/log/.kernel_tcp_key = b64 'SuperSecret', networking.service NETWORK_KEY=retXORFrg, /etc/.hosts_metadata 'ment12345') do not even reassemble the real key 'SuperSecretXORKeyFragment12345'. The dump is irrelevant to the repair, and /proc/sys is not changed by the damage. This wastes effort but does not break the reward.

defects.evidence: The graded tests depend only on cryptography's _rust.abi3.so. ldd shows it links no libcrypto: OpenSSL is statically linked. The run: restore only _rust.abi3.so (from the pip-cache wheel) and run_tests.sh reports 14 passed. Meanwhile the conda env's libcrypto.so.3 (3 overwritten spots) and the system /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.3 (3 overwritten spots) stay corrupted, and `ssh-keygen -t rsa` still segfaults (rc 139). The instruction explicitly complains about ssh-keygen. The whole 'five fragments' libcrypto recovery puzzle is never graded.

The damage the tests see (_rust.abi3.so, 16 bytes at file offsets 0x40b590 and 0x40b910 in .text) has no backup, and the instruction and hint never mention it. The planted fragments reconstruct only the conda libcrypto (I verified: the bz2 decompresses to 5172040 bytes, which differ from the damaged file in exactly 24 bytes). Recovery works only because /root/.cache/pip/http-v2/6/e/5/8/f/6e58...b293.body happens to be the cryptography-43.0.3 wheel (cmp: only the 16 damaged bytes differ); /opt/miniconda3 base also has cryptography 41.0.7. So the task is solvable offline, but by luck, not by design.

The system libcrypto (libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.18) has no backup and /var/cache/apt/archives has no .deb, so an exact repair of ssh-keygen is impossible offline. Only a workaround exists: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/miniconda3/lib ssh-keygen` works (rc 0). This is ungraded, so it does not hurt the reward, but the instruction's goal cannot be fully met.

The fragments (sshd_config, /tmp/.hidden_rsa_part2, /tmp/.hex_fragment_3_hint, /etc/environment, auth.log, plus the /root/recovery_hint.txt riddle) are a deliberately planted base64+bzip2 backup of the original conda libcrypto. It is a readable copy, but of a file the grader does not depend on, so it does not hand over the graded repair. I did not count it.

safety_note: The damage uses dd on shared libraries inside the image only. The repair copies .so files within the container. Nothing is host-escaping. Note: printf under /bin/sh wrote the literal text '\x00\x00' rather than NUL bytes, but it corrupts the files all the same.
